Crocodile Tteokbokki is a place I used to frequent as a student, but has now become a famous restaurant!
If you order the medium flavor, it tastes just like the cozy neighborhood tteokbokki, and if you order it as a filling, it comes mixed with fried food and served in a large pot. The texture of the rice cake is definitely very soft and chewy, making it taste even more special!
I went there around 4:10 after the weekend break, and it was full of people due to the open run, so I had to wait about 15 minutes to get in.
It's a system where you order in advance at a kiosk and wait outside, but first-time visitors tend to just wait if they don't know much, so it would be nice to see improvements in this area! Planning to go again next time :)

I visited because I had a Sunday lunch meeting.
It opens at 2pm on Sundays, so we arrived around 2:30pm. I heard there was usually a wait, but because it was early, I ended up being the second customer.
For my first order, I was told that I had to order at least 2 servings of charcoal grilled chicken ribs first, so I ordered 2 servings first.
Cut the charcoal grilled chicken ribs, green onions, and chili peppers and arrange them nicely. Instead of ssam vegetables, I recommended grilling seaweed on charcoal and wrapping it with grilled seaweed.
I ate charcoal grilled chicken ribs wrapped with grilled seaweed, mushroom wasabi, gungsaeng, and radish to suit my taste, and it was delicious.
You can refill any side dishes, seaweed, etc. that you run out of at the self-service bar.
I added 2 servings of charcoal grilled chicken ribs and truffle oil scallops, and it was even better when I ate them with scallops.
It is said that for chicken neck meat, the grill needs to be replaced with a different one. I heard that I could order 1 serving of soy sauce and 1 serving of seasoning, so I ate them one by one and it was delicious.
Hanyang University branch is holding a corn cheese Naver receipt event. Please note that if you perform the event at checkout, the corn cheese price will be deducted.
It was my first visit, and my companions were also satisfied.
We decided to get together early and go for a second meal, so we decided to eat crab ramen and soybean paste hotpot on our next visit.

Cost-effective Korean beef Oma Kase offers 7-8 types of top-quality Korean beef and is a place where you can enjoy a very high-quality beef feast.

It is often compared to Apgujeong-dong Miu, but each has its own charm. While Miu is closer to Korean-style beef, this place feels closer to steak-style grilling.

It is set up so that you can finish the course without biting into the greasy beef if you eat it with various side dishes, and the Japanese curry and ramen with plenty of Korean beef are the main culprits for stomach bombs.

It might be a good idea to give up your disguise on the day you visit.

I went on a Friday and my group got there early and there was a wait.

For alcohol, we paid a corkage fee for a bottle of white wine (10,000 won).
We finished it off with soju later.

To start, they serve raw oysters and bossam kimchi filling.
I immediately ate a piece of raw oyster with a glass of alcohol.
The steamed oysters come out in great shape.
What can I say about steamed oysters?
The oysters were a good size and the smell of the sea was good.
We brought Tabasco sauce separately.

reviews.author: Chanwook Lee
reviews.text:
One of the reasons I am grateful to be born in Korea is the fact that I can eat as many oysters as I want at a relatively low price. I wonder if there is any other country other than our country where people pile up and eat oysters in the winter.

I thought it was too early, but I stopped by to eat steamed oysters because I knew this winter wouldn't just end there. Since steaming oysters started on November 1st, it is clear that it will become more and more difficult to walk.

The menu is centered around oysters, but since it is a seasonal food, there are also alternative menu items such as steamed seafood and yeonpotang. However, the purpose of the visit was clear, so the two of us ordered a small bowl of steamed oysters.

It was a nice opportunity to be with my training camp classmates, so I paid 20,000 won and got a corkage for a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, which is a crazy pairing with steamed oysters. It was a Chilean wine, and I was surprised that it had better minerals than the New World wine.

Before the steamed oysters, raw oysters, fried pollack shells, and seaweed soup were served, and it was smart to prepare steamed oysters after eating them all. The fried pollack skin was sweet and crispy like seaweed bugak, so it naturally invited beer.

The raw oysters were also sweet and fragrant and fresh, but one thing that was disappointing was that the seeds were small. It is sold separately as a full or half plate, and if the seeds had been bigger, I would have ordered one without hesitation.

There was a generous amount of oysters, so I tried them on cabbage and raw radish, and the samhap was exceptionally delicious because the raw radish was done well. Still, the most impressive thing is the natural taste of oysters when nothing is added.

Steamed oysters are served in a large steamer and are prepared by opening and securing the lid on the table. It is already steamed so you can eat it right away, but you must always wear work gloves and plastic gloves to avoid burns.

The way to eat it is to find a gap in the shell, insert a knife into it, turn it half a turn, and the mouth opens. It's not difficult once you get the hang of it. The oysters revealed in this way were filled with warmth in their white flesh.

The yield was somewhat disappointing as it was not the peak oyster season, but to conclude, the taste of the oysters themselves was truly excellent. The sweetness was evident, just like its plump shape, and at the same time, it was accompanied by a heavy savory flavor.

The oyster juice that flowed out of the shell was almost like soup, and the saltiness of the shell contained it, giving it a salty taste that contrasted with the taste of the oyster. A sip of oyster juice, a sip of alcohol, and a chopstick of raw radish vegetable. This combination was really good.

I didn't dip anything except the last remaining oyster, but out of courtesy, I took a dip in the chojang. However, because of the moisture in the oysters, the vinegar didn't stick well, so it wasn't a good combination to begin with.

After eating steamed oysters, it is time to eat eggs steamed in the steamer. Perhaps because the eggs were filled with oysters, they were particularly delicious even though they were nothing special, and because they were steamed eggs, the taste was slightly different from boiled eggs.

The overall characteristic was that it had a subtle smoky flavor, and the egg white had an impressive soft texture. However, since the yolk is thicker than a boiled egg, it is recommended to add a little oyster juice.

I went in mid-winter, late November, during oyster season, and waited for about an hour to get in. They provided me with raw oysters as a main dish, so I was able to enjoy a glass of oyster wrap while waiting for the steamed oysters.
Steamed oysters are served in a large stainless steel steamer with an egg cooked in the middle. The oysters, which were kept warm and eaten right away, had very plump eggs inside and were really delicious when dipped in wasabi and vinegar. It was really good as a soju snack. It was enough for three people to eat.
I also ordered oyster kalguksu and it came with cabbage kimchi. The combination of kalguksu noodles, oysters, and cabbage kimchi was so delicious that I couldn't help but eat it even if I was full.
The seafood and green onion pancakes came out perfectly crispy and grilled as if deep-fried, and the texture was so interesting that I had to put in more effort.
The wait was terrible and it was so busy that it was difficult to call the waiters in between, but I was very satisfied with the taste. I also ate raw oysters, but I didn't get norovirus because I washed them thoroughly.

reviews.text:
One-line review: If you want to enjoy the best pork with clean, friendly service around Wangsimni...

These days, the standard has been raised to the point that it is more difficult to find a place that cooks meat tastelessly. The taste of the meat is guaranteed as standard, and the popularity of the store seems to be determined by what Plus Alpha is.

A little different from other meat restaurants, this place has a cast iron grill with good heat, a savory sauce made with a mixture of marinade and cutlassfish sauce, and carefully prepared and delicious sauces and side dishes that go well with the meat and are not made in a wasted manner. Soft tofu stew that was too tasty to be served as a service...
A system in which skilled staff grills meat from start to finish is a common feature of all popular meat restaurants...
When I brought children with me, I could immediately understand why this place was famous and why there was always a lot of people waiting as I saw them cut the children's meat into smaller pieces and place it in front of them even without a separate request.

The clean atmosphere of the store and the friendly service make it one of the best pork restaurants I've ever been to.

No matter what part or dish I ordered on the menu, it exceeded my expectations. In particular, the soybean paste rice bowl I ordered after eating the meat was the best, both in terms of quantity and taste...

If you go without a reservation, the wait may be very long, so be sure to make a reservation if possible.

One-line review: A clean shabu-shabu restaurant where you can cook and eat according to each individual’s taste.

Since it just opened, it is bright and clean overall. The tables were larger and more spacious than regular restaurants, which was nice because each person had their own induction stove installed.
You can choose from a variety of soup bases depending on your taste, and I also like the fact that you can keep adding vegetables, meat, noodles, etc., so you can eat both.
In particular, since the child cooked and ate shabu-shabu himself, there was an added advantage that the meal was fun and there was no need to play cell phone videos.

The sauce, base, and meat quality were all satisfactory. You can continue to add soup for free.

For your information, I think eating porridge boiled in soybean paste shabu tastes better than other soup bases... If you are going to eat porridge, I recommend going with a group and having one person order soybean paste shabu.

It's a place with easy parking, friendly service, and good value for money, so there's nothing to regret. I think I will visit often ^^

p.s. Since the table is limited to 4 people, it may be difficult to use the port if you are dining with a group of more than that (especially if there are an odd number of people)...

reviews.text:
*Ordinary Gyukatsu restaurant

It's located inside Entersix, so it's easy to park and use. Parking fees are also deducted from the usage amount.

In the case of Gyukatsu meat, it is basic to remove the tendons, but perhaps that was not done well, and sometimes there are tough parts.
The taste isn't that bad, but it's not special either. Mazesoba is refreshing and delicious.
The sanitary conditions of the brazier are mediocre, the fire power is weak, so it takes a long time to cook, and there is no sizzling sound. At other Gyukatsu restaurants, the temperature is so high that it makes a sizzling sound, but I'm not sure if that's intentional...
The sauce is soy sauce similar to horse sauce and there is no salt. When it comes to Gyukatsu, salt is essential, but this is a strange part.
You can also add rice for 1,000 won, but it seems unnecessary since they serve more rice than other Japanese restaurants.
